messages:
Maria: Heads-up — trying to spin up the new p4d pool in us-east-1 and the autoscaler keeps failing during the network bootstrap. Logs show API throttling on security-group calls.

Maria: Example error from the autoscaler:
```
ERROR: Client.RequestLimitExceeded: Request limit exceeded for ModifySecurityGroups
  at AmazonEC2.modifySecurityGroups (ec2_client.go:312)
  at autoscaler/network.go:87
```

Josh: Ugh, I saw that pattern last week. AWS had a burst throttle on EC2 for our account after the scripted SG creation during blue-green. Are we creating lots of unique SGs per deploy?

Maria: Yeah, the provisioning job creates per-cluster ephemeral SGs (one per node group) + we add pod-level rules. When we scale to 40 nodes the controller issues hundreds of ModifySecurityGroups calls in a few mins.

Anya: @Maria can you file an AWS support case and ask for EC2 API rate-limit increase and for an exception on ModifySecurityGroups throttling? Also ask limits for security-groups-per-network-interface. Provide the support team with the timestamps & request IDs.

Maria: Filed case 1234567891 with AWS, included request IDs and recent CloudTrail snippets. Case summary: "EC2 API throttle causing node provisioning failures for GPU fleet (p4d) in us-east-1)"

infra-bot: Notice: New support case 1234567891 created by Maria. Estimated response time: 6–12 hours.

Josh: Short-term workaround: stop creating SGs per node. Can we switch the templated SG model and pre-create a small pool of reusable SGs (eg sg-gpu-01..04) and assign them to nodes? That would cut API pressure.

Olly: We can also batch the calls in the autoscaler to reduce ModifySecurityGroups frequency. But that's a code change — could take a day. Reusable SGs is faster.

Anya: Also ask AWS for a soft limit raise on "Request rate for RunInstances/ModifySecurityGroups" and increase on "security-groups per ENI" if applicable. Include expected burst rates: we hit ~250 SG ops/min during rollout windows.

Maria: AWS replied (initial): investigating, flagged for EC2 team. Their suggestion: reduce concurrent SG modifications or use CloudFormation to make fewer API calls. They asked for our expected concurrency & business impact.

Josh: Can someone put together a short summary for the AWS case: account id, region, service (EC2), API names, peak ops/min, sample request IDs and stack traces. I'll paste it into the case.

Maria: Pasted details and asked for an emergency increase. Also attached a short timeline showing failed node launches: 2026-03-17T09:12Z — 09:20Z (multiple failures).

Olly: Ops note — for immediate deploys we can serialise node creation in the autoscaler (throttle ourselves) so it doesn't blow past AWS API limits. Set concurrency cap to 5 nodes/min. We should also add exponential backoff on ModifySecurityGroups errors.

cloud-support: AWS support updated case 1234567891: "We can provisionally increase API burst allowance for 48 hours while you implement mitigation. Need confirmation of contact and ticket owner."

Anya: Confirm accept, ask them to extend to 72h. Also request that they coordinate with the EC2 team to monitor throttles.

Maria: Confirmed 72h and added contact details (maria@redwood.com, eng-infra pager).

Josh: Follow-ups: 1) Implement reusable SGs today. 2) Autoscaler change to throttle/batch ModifySecurityGroups next sprint. 3) Add CloudFormation/Terraform pre-apply for infra changes to avoid API storms. 4) Monitor CloudTrail + Service Quotas dashboard for >80% usage alerts.

Olly: I'll open a quick PR to switch the nodegroup provisioning to use a pool of 6 pre-created SGs and add a feature flag so we can roll it out behind a toggle.

Maria: Thanks — will update thread when AWS confirms permanent limit change. For now mark the p4d rollout paused until we flip the flag. :hourglass:
